name: clustering_coefficient
author: 219c8a12
description: Measures how tightly knit a node's neighbourhood is with the local clustering coefficient: the fraction of pairs of a node's neighbours that are themselves connected (0 = none, 1 = all; nodes with fewer than 2 neighbours score 0). Use for questions like 'how tightly knit is Alice's circle?', 'do X's friends know each other?' or 'which nodes sit in dense clusters?'. Give a node id for that node's score, or omit it to get the top_k most clustered nodes. The summary always reports the graph-wide average clustering and the global transitivity (3 x triangles / connected triples, a different measure). Works on any graph: directed graphs are treated as undirected and weights are ignored. Returns a list of nodes with score (the coefficient), degree and triangles.

graph_id.description: Id of the graph to analyse.

node.description: Optional node id (not a name; use lookup_node to find it). If given, returns only this node's coefficient plus the graph average.

top_k.description: When no node is given, how many of the most clustered nodes to return.

min_degree.description: When ranking, only consider nodes with at least this many neighbours (2 by default; raise it to skip trivial 1.0 scores of low-degree nodes). Does not affect the average.
